'''''Euphorbia epithymoides''''', the '''cushion spurge''', [[synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] ''E. polychroma'', is a [[species]] of [[deciduous]] [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Euphorbiaceae, [[native plant|native]] to Libya, Turkey and East, Middle, and Southeast Europe. It is a compact, clump-forming, [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|45|cm|0|abbr=on}}, bearing terminal [[cyme (botany)|cyme]]s of acid yellow flower-heads ([[cyathia]]) in spring and summer.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> The [[cultivar]] 'Major'<ref>{{cite web|title=''Euphorbia epithymoides'' 'Major' AGM|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/332109/Euphorbia-epithymoides-Major/Details |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=25 June 2020}}</ref> has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].

==Taxonomy==
''Euphorbia epithymoides'' was named by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1762. It is classified in the genus ''[[Euphorbia]]'' within the wider [[Euphorbiaceae]] family and has three accepted [[subspecies]].<ref name="POWO">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=346404-1 |title=''Euphorbia epithymoides'' L. |access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref>

* ''Euphorbia epithymoides'' subsp. ''epithymoides'' – Native to central Europe from Germany to the northwestern Balkan Peninsula<ref name="POWO subsp epithymoides">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=3311322-4 |title=''Euphorbia epithymoides'' subsp. ''epithymoides'' |access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref>
* ''Euphorbia epithymoides'' subsp. ''gregersenii'' – Native to Gostović Valley in Bosnia and Hercegovina<ref name="POWO subsp gregersenii">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=77350424-1 |title=''Euphorbia epithymoides'' subsp. ''gregersenii'' (K.Malý ex Beck) Frajman |access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref>
* ''Euphorbia epithymoides'' subsp. ''lingulata'' – Native to Eastern Europe from Ukraine southwards to Greece and northwestern Turkey<ref name="POWO subsp lingulata">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=77256535-1 |title=''Euphorbia epithymoides'' subsp. ''lingulata'' (Heuff.) Nyman |access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref>
